question: Should OpenClaw Core own and ship a durable Pi/Review/Git-promotion orchestration boundary backed by a vendored contracts artifact?
rationale: This is a new Core product and trust boundary, not a mechanical bug fix; deciding its permanent owner, external-service contract, and dependency provenance requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Do not add this Core boundary
options.body: Keep orchestration and its contracts in the owning platform/service repository until OpenClaw has a maintainer-approved generic integration need.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow Core design
options.body: Approve a documented Core ownership and security model, then require a typed source-reviewed contract package, scoped entrypoint, and upgrade-safe proof before merge.

options.title: Extract a plugin or external integration
options.body: Keep OpenClaw Core generic and implement the optional platform workflow through an existing plugin or external-service seam if those APIs are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Do not add this Core boundary
recommendation.body: Keep orchestration and its contracts in the owning platform/service repository until OpenClaw has a maintainer-approved generic integration need.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence default routing candidate for a repository-level Core product-boundary decision.
